title: Smooth complete local functors are power series extensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $B\to A$ be a continuous local $k$-algebra homomorphism of complete Noetherian local rings with residue fields identified with $k$, inducing the identity on these residue fields [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For an Artinian local $k$-algebra $R$ with residue field $k$ put $h_A(R)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k,\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{cont}}(A,R)$ and define $h_B$ similarly; Artinian means that descending chains of ideals stabilize. The transformation $h_A\to h_B$ is formally smooth if for every surjection $R'\twoheadrightarrow R$ with square-zero kernel the map $h_A(R')\to h_A(R)\times_{h_B(R)}h_B(R')$ is surjective. This condition holds if and only if $A$ is isomorphic, as a complete local $B$-algebra, to $B[[u_1,\ldots,u_r]]$, where $r=\dim_k\mathfrak m_A/(\mathfrak m_BA+\mathfrak m_A^2)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The relative tangent space of $h_A\to h_B$ is the dual of this quotient. In particular, an unobstructed functor prorepresented by $A$ over $k$ has $A\cong k[[t_1,\ldots,t_N]]$, with $N$ the dimension of its tangent space; unobstructed means that every element lifts across each such square-zero surjection.

source.place: Tag 06HL (lemma-smooth-morphism-power-series); tangent-space quotient in example-tangent-space-map-prorepresentable-functor. The square-zero test is equivalent to the arbitrary Artinian-surjection test by factoring through the powers of the nilpotent kernel.

proof.text: For an Artinian local $R$, [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] gives $\mathfrak m_R^N=0$, hence maximal-ideal-adic completeness: the inverse system is eventually constantly $R$. If $R^\prime\twoheadrightarrow R$ has kernel $J$, then $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_{R^\prime}$ is nilpotent. Factor it as $R^\prime/J^{j+1}\twoheadrightarrow R^\prime/J^j$, $j\geq1$, ending at $R^\prime$. Each kernel $J^j/J^{j+1}$ squares to zero since $2j\geq j+1$. Inductively apply the assumed square-zero lifting property, using the fixed map $B\to R^\prime$ at every stage. Thus the test in the statement implies the test for arbitrary Artinian surjections; the reverse implication just restricts the tests.

source.place: Tag 06HL and remark-compare-smooth-schlessinger; reduction to square-zero kernels

proof.text: Put $T=B[[X_1,\ldots,X_r]]$ and $N=(X_1,\ldots,X_r)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring], $T$ is Noetherian local. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-quotient-variables], $\ker(T\to B)=N$, so its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_BT+N$ and its residue field is $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-complete-over-complete-base] it is $\mathfrak n$-adically complete. These facts hold also for $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 06HL, proof: the auxiliary ring T=R[[X_1,...,X_n]]

proof.text: First assume $A=T$ as a complete local $B$-algebra. Given an Artinian surjection $R^\prime\twoheadrightarrow R$, a map $A\to R$ and a compatible map $B\to R^\prime$, lift each image of $X_i$ to $b_i\in R^\prime$. The residue fields agree, so $b_i\in\mathfrak m_{R^\prime}$. Step 1 gives completeness of $R^\prime$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] with coefficient ring $B$, target $R^\prime$, ideal $\mathfrak m_{R^\prime}$ and values $b_i$. Its map is local since it sends $\mathfrak m_B$ and every $X_i$ into $\mathfrak m_{R^\prime}$, and is therefore continuous for maximal-ideal topologies. Reduction to $R$ has the original constants and variable values; evaluation uniqueness makes it the prescribed map $A\to R$. This solves the lifting problem. A complete local $B$-algebra isomorphism $A\cong T$ transports this construction by composition.

source.place: Tag 06HL, proof, forward implication: lift variable images

proof.text: Conversely assume formal smoothness. Set $V=\mathfrak m_A/(\mathfrak m_BA+\mathfrak m_A^2)$. It is finite-dimensional: the finite ideal generators of $\mathfrak m_A$ span its quotient over $k$, since $\mathfrak m_A$ annihilates this quotient [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Choose $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in\mathfrak m_A$ lifting a basis of $V$. Set $K=\mathfrak m_BT+\mathfrak n^2$. There are $B$-algebra identifications $A/(\mathfrak m_BA+\mathfrak m_A^2)=k\oplus V$ and $T/K=k\oplus k^r$, with multiplication $(a,v)(b,w)=(ab,aw+bv)$. For the first, use the given coefficient map $k\to A$ and write each element uniquely as its residue plus an element of $\mathfrak m_A$; products of two such latter elements vanish in the quotient. For the second, constant and linear coefficients give the displayed decomposition, and [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with $J=0,n=2$ identifies series with zero constant and linear coefficients with $N^2\subseteq\mathfrak n^2$. Terms from $\mathfrak m_B$ vanish as well. Sending the classes of $x_i$ to those of $X_i$ gives an isomorphism between these two square-zero $k$-algebras. Denote the resulting map $A\to T/K$ by $f_0$. Independence follows by reading constant and linear coefficients: elements of $\mathfrak m_BT+\mathfrak n^2$ have those coefficients in $\mathfrak m_B$, so no nonzero residue or linear class is killed.

source.place: Tag 06HL, proof, converse: basis of the relative cotangent space and f_1

proof.text: The map $T/\mathfrak n^2\twoheadrightarrow T/K$ has square-zero kernel, because $\mathfrak n^2\subseteq K\subseteq\mathfrak n$. For $n\geq2$, the maps $T/\mathfrak n^{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow T/\mathfrak n^n$ have square-zero kernels since $2n\geq n+1$. All these rings are Artinian local with residue field $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local], applied to the Noetherian local ring from step 2. Formal smoothness therefore lifts $f_0$ first to $f_2:A\to T/\mathfrak n^2$ and recursively to compatible local $B$-algebra maps $f_n:A\to T/\mathfrak n^n$. Put $f_1$ equal to the residue map. Completeness [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] identifies the compatible values $(f_n(a))_n$ with a unique element $f(a)\in T$. Coordinatewise addition and multiplication prove that $f:A\to T$ is a $B$-algebra homomorphism. Its residue is the identity on $k$, so it is local and sends $\mathfrak m_A^n$ into $\mathfrak n^n$, proving continuity. Modulo $K$ it equals $f_0$, hence its relative cotangent map over $B$ is the chosen basis isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06HL, proof, converse: compatible lifts and their inverse limit

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-complete-local-cotangent-surjectivity] to $f:A\to T$ with coefficient base $C=B$. Step 2 and the hypotheses on $A,B$ supply completeness, Noetherianity and the common residue field; step 5 supplies the relative cotangent isomorphism. Thus $f$ is surjective. Choose $y_i\in A$ with $f(y_i)=X_i$. Since $f$ induces the identity on residue fields, $y_i\in\mathfrak m_A$. Evaluation [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] gives a $B$-algebra map $s:T\to A$, $X_i\mapsto y_i$. It is local and continuous since $\mathfrak n$ is generated by $\mathfrak m_B$ and the variables. The composite $f\circ s$ fixes constants and all $X_i$, so evaluation uniqueness makes it $\mathrm{id}_T$. On relative cotangent spaces, $\overline f\,\overline s=1$ and $\overline f$ is an isomorphism, hence $\overline s=\overline f^{-1}$. Apply the same cotangent criterion to $s$ over $B$; it is surjective. It is also injective, since $f\circ s=1$. Hence $s$ is a $B$-algebra isomorphism, whose inverse $f$ is continuous, as required.

source.place: Tags 06HL and 06GZ: surjectivity of f, construction of a section, surjectivity of the section

proof.text: The relative tangent space means the fibre over the constant map $B\to k\to D$ of $h_A(D)\to h_B(D)$, where $D=k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. A local $k$-map $g:A\to D$ is uniquely $g(a)=\overline a+\epsilon d(a)$; multiplication says $d(ab)=\overline a\,d(b)+\overline b\,d(a)$ and $k$-linearity says $d|_k=0$. Thus $d$ kills $\mathfrak m_A^2$; being over the constant map from $B$ says it kills $\mathfrak m_BA$. Conversely any $k$-linear $\lambda:V\to k$ gives such a map by $a\mapsto\overline a+\epsilon\lambda(a-\overline a)$, where the specified coefficient field lifts $\overline a$ to $A$. The displayed multiplication rule verifies it is a homomorphism. It kills $\mathfrak m_A^2$, so is continuous. These constructions are mutually inverse and preserve addition and scalar multiplication. This identifies the relative tangent space with $V^\vee$ and gives dimension $r$.

source.place: Tag 06ST (example-tangent-space-map-prorepresentable-functor), with the square-zero calculation written out

proof.text: For an unobstructed functor prorepresented by $A$, its natural identifications with $h_A$ turn unobstructedness into the square-zero lifting property for $h_A\to h_k$, since $h_k(R)$ is a singleton. Apply the equivalence proved above with $B=k$. Now $\mathfrak m_B=0$, so step 7 identifies its tangent space with $(\mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak m_A^2)^\vee$, of dimension $N$. The power series extension is therefore $k[[t_1,\ldots,t_N]]$. This includes $N=0$, for which the ring is $k$.

Step 1 reduces arbitrary Artinian surjections to square-zero ones via the J^j filtration. Step 2 gives T=B[[X]]: Noetherian, local with maximal ideal m_B T+N, complete (quotient-variables, complete-over-complete-base). Step 3 builds the lift by adic evaluation into the complete ring R', and uniqueness gives the prescribed reduction. Step 4 identifies A/(m_B A+m_A^2) with T/K as k⊕V, using combined-ideal-coefficients at J=0, n=2. Step 5 lifts compatibly along square-zero quotients, which are Artinian by noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local, and takes the inverse limit. Step 6 applies 06GZ to f, builds the section s by evaluation, gets fs=id by uniqueness, and applies 06GZ again to s. Step 7 is the dual-numbers derivation computation. Step 8 is the case B=k. Every cited statement says what each step takes from it. New node lem-sfb-complete-local-cotangent-surjectivity is 06GZ (1)<=>(3) with base C; it is self-contained and statement-only.
